newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK housing block blaze kills seven, injures 28.
newsitem.headline: HK housing block blaze kills seven, injures 28.

text.p: Residents squatted on window ledges and clung to drainpipes to escape a fire that killed at least seven people, including two babies, in a residential building in Hong Kong on Tuesday.
The fire broke out at lunchtime on the sixth floor of a 20-storey block in Kowloon district, and spread to a lower floor. Firefighters took four hours to quell the blaze.
The dead were two baby girls, four women -- one of them aged 65 -- and one man.
"They died from inhaling a lot of thick smoke. They did not die from burns. Their burns were quite minor," said a doctor at one of two hospitals taking the casualties.
A government spokeswoman said at least 28 people also were injured, including a fireman, and had been taken to hospital.
"The fire has been put out, 28 have been injured by the fire and their conditions are still unknown," the spokeswoman said.
A hospital spokesman said the fireman was in satisfactory condition.

At the height of the fire, terrified residents overcome by smoke on the upper floors clung to external pipes and scrambled onto ledges and flimsy clothes driers, shouting out to firemen in frantic scenes relayed live by television.
Firemen ferried swooning housewives and howling children -- even a dog -- down an extension ladder to safety.

The cause of the fire was not immediately known. But district police chief Bonnie Smith told reporters that one theory was that it might have been started by a cigarette and then have spread quickly because fire doors were not shut.
"Most of the smoke doors were left open, and this is believed to be what caused so many casualties," she said.
"According to witnesses at the scene, the fire is believed to have started from an inadvertently discarded cigarette butt."
Hong Kong has suffered some of its worst building fires in recent months, including two major disasters.
In November, a fire in a building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street killed 39 people and injured 81.
A fire in a karaoke bar in January killed 17 people in Kowloon's Tsimshatsui entertainment district.
